sections.name: File setup, StageStatus
sections.title: Imports and status names
sections.what: Loads the tools for state, icons, the finding helpers and the observable work view, and defines the allowed status names.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A new status name that is not in the list will still display, but with raw text.

sections.name: TrackStage
sections.title: Shape of one stage
sections.what: Describes what each stage row carries: its name, icon, fixed purpose text, status, times, summary, log, optional body, findings, replay limit and running note.
sections.why: The purpose field is documented as a fixed description, not live activity.
sections.watch_out: The replay limit is only used during replay, so a live view ignores it.

sections.name: WORD, word, code
sections.title: Plain status words and short codes
sections.what: Maps each status to a plain English label such as Complete, In progress or Failed, and a short code for styling.
sections.why: Likely reason: the owner reads plain words, while the short codes let the page colour each state.
sections.watch_out: Any status not in this list is turned into text by replacing underscores with spaces.

sections.name: StageTrack (part 1)
sections.title: Choosing the stage to show
sections.what: Forces stages that are still running to show as interrupted when the run is no longer active, then picks the stage that most needs attention, falling back to the last completed stage.
sections.why: The header says a leftover running row is shown as interrupted, never as live.
sections.watch_out: The order of checks decides which stage is shown, so changing it changes what the owner sees first.

sections.name: StageTrack: if
sections.title: Following the live stage and announcing changes
sections.what: Keeps the chosen stage in view while the current stage moves, unless the owner has picked another. Announces each real status change for screen readers, then works out the selected stage, the completed count, its findings, raw record and duration. Renders the header and the Follow live stage link.
sections.why: The comments say announcements come only from real changes in the props.
sections.watch_out: Announcements fire only when the set of statuses changes, so a stage that changes twice quickly may be announced once.

sections.name: StageTrack (part 3)
sections.title: Stage list and selected stage header
sections.what: Draws the list of stages, each with an icon, label, status code and times. Below it shows the chosen stage's path, label, purpose, start time, finish or waiting note, and duration.
sections.why: The list lets the owner move between stages, and the header states where the stage sits in the run.
sections.watch_out: Missing times appear as placeholders, so a blank time may mean the server did not record it.

sections.name: StageTrack (part 4)
sections.title: Stage body, notes and retry
sections.what: Shows a note for a stage that has not started, then the findings, any custom body, the observable work, and notes for missing, running, interrupted, failed or insufficient-evidence stages. Failed stages get a retry button when retry is allowed. A collapsible raw record shows the log and summary.
sections.why: The notes are written so the owner knows whether the stage is waiting, stopped or missing data.
sections.watch_out: The retry button appears only for failed stages, so an insufficient-evidence stage needs a different action.

summary: The pipeline trace: a list of analysis stages with their status, times, findings and raw record, where the owner picks a stage to read.
purpose: Shows how far a run has got, what each stage found, and why a stage failed or stopped.
why: The header says it renders only what the stage records carry, with no timer and no made-up activity. This is stated in the code.
how: 1. Marks any stage still shown as running as interrupted when the run is not active. 2. Chooses the current stage: the first running, interrupted, failed or insufficient one, otherwise the last completed one. 3. Follows the current stage unless the owner picks another. 4. Announces status changes for screen readers. 5. Shows the chosen stage's times, findings, observable work, notes, retry button and raw record.
inputs: The list of stages with their status, times, summary, log and optional body, plus flags for retry, active run and labels.
outputs: A stage list, a detail card for the chosen stage, and a retry button when allowed.
risks: A stage left in a running state after a crash is shown as interrupted, so the owner must check the run before assuming it is live. A retry is offered only for failed stages, not for insufficient-evidence stages.
debug: If the wrong stage is shown, check the order of statuses used to pick the current stage. If no findings appear, check that the summary has the expected fields. If the retry button is missing, check the retry flag and the stage status.
